cards: アメリカーノ（ブラックコーヒー）
すみません、注文に間違いがあると思います。
ミルク入りコーヒーではなく、アメリカーノを注文しました。
菓子パンが一つ足りません。
取り替えていただけますか。
こちらが私のレシートです。
注文を確認していただけますか。
cardGlosses: pastry (sweet bread; contextual rendering of pan dulce)
Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order.
I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk.
I am missing a pastry. (lit. one pastry is short)
Can you change it for me, please?
Can you check my order, please?
reader: カウンターに着いて、アメリカーノと菓子パンを注文します。
その後、ウェイターがミルク入りコーヒーを一杯くれます。
かばんを確認して、菓子パンがないことに気づきます。
まず、ほほえんでこう言います。「すみません、注文に間違いがあると思います。」
次に、こう説明します。「ミルク入りコーヒーではなく、アメリカーノを注文しました。」
さらに、こう言います。「菓子パンが一つ足りません。そして、こちらが私のレシートです。」
こうたずねます。「取り替えていただけますか。」
ウェイターがこう言います。「かしこまりました。すぐにコーヒーと菓子パンをお持ちします。」
readerGlosses: I get to the counter and order an americano and a pastry.
Then the server (waiter) gives me a cup of coffee with milk.
I check my bag and see that there is no pastry.
First, I smile and say: "Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order."
Then I explain: "I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk."
I also say: "I am missing a pastry, and here is my receipt."
I ask: "Can you change it for me, please?"
The server (waiter) says: "Of course, I will bring you the coffee and the pastry now."
concerns: This is an unreviewed draft, not validated Japanese and not a qualified approval. Native-speaker review is still required. No files were edited.

ACCEPTED (critique 1, 10, 18): mesero is now ウェイター in card 8 and reader lines 2 and 8. Japanese has the gendered pair ウェイター/ウェイトレス, so the earlier claim that Japanese cannot mark this was wrong; the mesera counterpart is ウェイトレス. This also removes the 男性の店員/店員 split.
OPEN (server term): the scene is at a counter, where 店員 would be the realistic word, but the source term is server (male), so ウェイター was kept. Reviewer should decide.
REJECTED (critique 2, 17, wording): すみませんが or お願いします was not added to cards 14 and 16. The 〜ていただけますか request form already carries por favor without a literal word. The glosses now restore 'please'.
NOTED (critique 2, register): 〜ていただけますか is a step more polite than usted + puede. It was kept as normal customer-to-staff speech; reviewer may prefer 〜てもらえますか.
Japanese has no tú/usted pronoun contrast. The usted note is handled by です/ます and the honorific request forms.

REJECTED (critique 3): 私の was kept in こちらが私のレシートです because the source says mi recibo. It is grammatical but slightly explicit; レシートはこちらです or こちらがレシートです is a more natural option for the reviewer. The gloss is restored to 'Here is my receipt.'

REJECTED (critique 4): 菓子パンが入っていません would assume a bag and まだ来ていません would add 'not yet'; neither is in Me falta un pan dulce. 菓子パンが一つ足りません was kept, with the first-person gloss restored. Reviewer should confirm 足りません does not imply that other pastries arrived.

ACCEPTED (critique 5): glosses now use natural English that matches the source English. In card 12 and reader line 5 the Japanese puts the negated item first (ミルク入りコーヒーではなく、…), the reverse of the Spanish clause order; the meaning is unchanged.

REJECTED (critique 9): bolsa was not changed to 袋 or 紙袋. The source says only mi bolsa / my bag, and it is not known whether this is a takeout bag. かばん was kept, but it leans toward a personal bag and Japanese has no fully neutral word, so the reviewer should decide between かばん, バッグ and 袋.
Reader line 3 now reads 菓子パンがないことに気づきます to keep veo que no hay without adding 'in it'.
pan dulce stays 菓子パン as a contextual sweet pastry, not a specific item such as クロワッサン. Per critique 8, this is a localization: 菓子パン evokes Japanese items such as メロンパン and あんパン.
OPEN (coffee with milk): ミルク入りコーヒー was kept as the literal rendering. カフェオレ is the closest everyday term and カフェラテ may read as a different drink. Reviewer should decide.
NOTED (critique 6, 7): アメリカーノ was kept; アメリカン must not be used as an alternate because in Japan it usually means weak drip coffee. デカフェ was kept; カフェインレス is at least as common on menus.
ACCEPTED (critique 14): llego is now 着いて, with the gloss 'I get to'.
ACCEPTED (critique 12): また is replaced with さらに in line 6 to avoid the 'say again' reading. そして was added inside the quote for the source's 'y'.

ACCEPTED in part (critique 13): the colon before 「」 is replaced by こう言います。「…」, which keeps the source order of speech verb then quote. Every quote is a full sentence ending with 。 inside 」. Reviewer may prefer the 「…」と言います pattern.
Line 4 sonrío y digo is now ほほえんでこう言います, keeping two verbs instead of 笑顔で.

NOTED (critique 11): una taza de is rendered with the counter 一杯, so the card word カップ does not appear in the reader. カップ, テーブル and デカフェ do not appear in the source reader either, and no scene content was added to include them.
NOTED (critique 15): かしこまりました and すぐに…お持ちします were kept for Claro, ahora le traigo. かしこまりました is staff keigo closer to 'Certainly' than a literal 'Of course'; もちろんです is the more literal alternative.

NOTED (critique 16): the title 'Un pedido equivocado' has no field in the requested output, so it is not rendered. Suggested rendering is 間違った注文 (a wrong order), which is closer to the source than 注文の間違い.
